_scenario: EOLIANITE ABRASIVITY SIMULATION SET - client order 2026-08-16 (CR.5009 panel Q4 follow-up: no measured abrasivity figures exist; simulate with aeolian-limestone figures). Rock model: aeolian carbonate dune rock (eolianite/calcarenite) - soft porous calcite matrix (UCS 15-30, consistent with the 2026-08-15 soft-rock and porosity rulings) cementing WELL-ROUNDED ~200 um QUARTZ grains inherited from dune transport. The quartz, not the matrix, governs steel wear: it is the only phase harder than any tool steel. EVERY number below is [H] literature-anchored, pending the external tests (XRF/mineralogy, LCPC, Cerchar, Bond Ai on real samples).

quartz_pct._note: CLIENT DATUM 2026-08-16: 5 % silica at the zone-1 feed (supersedes the assistant [H] 20 % central of the same day; envelope [3-8] is a confirmation band around the client figure). XRF/mineralogy still CONFIRMS it and splits free quartz grains vs other silica forms

quartz_grain_um._note: [H] client statement: ~200 um very round grains

porosity_pct._note: [H] consistent with the porous-stone moisture set 12/15/11 %

hardness_frame._note: quartz > any steel -> hard-abrasive regime (Khrushchov): wear is quartz-governed; calcite < steel -> mild. Rounded grains shift two-body cutting toward three-body rolling wear - lower metal cutting rate (-20 % applied on LCPC) but polishing wear on teeth and severe wear on POLYMER media (screen mats) and high-velocity surfaces (fan, classifier wheel)

simulated_indices._rev: REV A 2026-08-16: recomputed at the CLIENT-DECLARED quartz 5 % (was assistant [H] 20 %)

cerchar_CAI._reliability: [H] CAI is UNRELIABLE on UCS < 25 MPa (pin ploughs the soft matrix instead of scratching) - quoted for completeness, LCPC governs

LCPC_ABR_g_per_t.class: low-abrasive, upper half of LCPC 0-500 'not very abrasive' - the quartz keeps it well above clean-limestone values (~100-200)
LCPC_ABR_g_per_t.basis: mixture rule quartz sand ~1700 g/t x 0.05 + soft limestone ~300 g/t x 0.95, minus ~20 % roundness allowance
LCPC_ABR_g_per_t._note: LCPC is THE right test for soft rock with hard fine grains - priority order over Cerchar

liberation_model._rev: REV B 2026-08-16 (4-expert silica team, client cookie clarification: grains embedded in the mass like chips in a cookie, never broken). The REV A ladder below is SUPERSEDED - it overstated liberation 3-35x.

cookie_law.form: L(x) = 1 for x <= d; ln(k*d/x)/ln(k) for d < x < k*d; 0 for x >= k*d

k.status: [H] random breakage of dilute round inclusions gives k~1.5-2; interface-preferential detachment in the porous weakly-cemented eolianite raises it to ~3-4 (and raises S_att - grains plucked whole)

cookie_law.structural_theorems: a closed loop cannot enrich its only exit; every cut >= 1.5 mm leaves BOTH sides at bulk grade (free grains travel with their 0.1-0.4 mm band). Only the SP.36 65 um cut discriminates quartz.

liberation_model._embedded_note: REV B tribology: the 0.3 embedded discount is WRONG for impactors (inertial backing makes an embedded-grain impact equal to a free-grain impact - CR.5011/CR.5113 severity raised); it remains valid for low-stress sliding (sandpaper particles POLISH, they do not cut: contact ~0.3-0.4 GPa vs steel plasticity onset ~1.8 GPa)

machine_severity_factors._note: [H] relative contact severity per machine class (velocity x pressure x steel/polymer sensitivity), used ONLY for ranking - not absolute life prediction

sizer_teeth_g_per_t._note: [H] REV A: order of magnitude for segment/tooth steel loss on ABR ~310 rock (was 2-8 g/t at the superseded 20 % quartz) - RFQ wear-guarantee anchor, replaced by vendor guarantees priced on the real LCPC result

product_quality_frame._note: quartz does not calcine and does not neutralize: CaCO3-based product values dilute by the quartz content of each product - the KFS (kiln feed) chemistry question is raised to the client explicitly
